title: Zoom in: reading a chat at LOCAL_QUORUM, one full read plus one digest
caption: Only one replica sends the rows; the other sends a hash. A mismatch triggers a repair before the answer goes back.

messages.label: last 50 of conv c7 (LOCAL_QUORUM)
messages.note: A single partition, read in clustering order (newest first).

messages.label: full read
messages.note: The fastest replica (by recent latency) sends the data.

messages.label: digest read
messages.note: Another replica only returns a hash of the same result, which saves bandwidth.

messages.label: digest
messages.note: The hashes match: two replicas agree.

scenarios.name: Digest mismatch
scenarios.summary: The two replicas disagree: fetch both full results, keep the newest cell, and fix the stale replica before answering.

messages.label: digest (differs)
messages.note: B missed a message while it was briefly down.

messages.label: full read
messages.note: Get B's full result and merge: the newest timestamp wins per cell.

messages.label: repair write
messages.note: Read repair: B gets the missing message.

scenarios.name: Replica A stalls
scenarios.summary: Don't wait for a slow replica: after its usual p99, ask another one (speculative retry).

messages.label: full read
messages.note: A is in a long GC pause and doesn't answer.

messages.label: full read (speculative)
messages.note: Sent once A takes longer than its p99.

messages.label: 50 messages
messages.note: A slow node adds a few ms instead of a timeout.

scenarios.name: Risk: read in another DC
scenarios.summary: LOCAL_QUORUM is only strong inside one DC. A user who writes in DC2 and reads in DC1 straight away may not see their message.

messages.label: INSERT msg (via DC2)
messages.note: The user's phone switched networks and reached the other region.

messages.label: mutation
messages.note: On its way to DC1, about 80 ms.

messages.label: last 50 of conv c7
messages.note: The next request lands in DC1 straight away.

messages.label: stale page
messages.note: Mitigate: pin each user to a home DC, or have the client show its own sent messages until they appear.
